utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. McCloskey, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes good morning, Mr. President, everyone. I just have a response to you on your question about what happened to the attestation for Witness RM144 that we filed quite late. And we -- we -- what we've been able to track down is that we got out of the gate on time, and it got attested relatively quickly with four others, and somehow when it came to filing the motion, the other four got filed on time, and this one somehow got put on a shelf and fell through the cracks. We think we got a friendly reminder phone call and -- in January, and so we found it and filed it in January where we obviously should have sought leave to file it late, which we did not. And that's the -- that's what I've been able to discover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The "somehow," of course, is the puzzling word. Mr. Lukic, you have ... you can say it is 1-0 so if you a somehow lost thing, we will consider a somehow explanation perhaps. Let's see whether you need it. Mr. Lukic, you wanted to raise a matter as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Regarding your question from yesterday, P1451, that was protected witness, I think so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shouldn't we then -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just can tell you that with -- the checkup done by the Prosecution is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, so then there's -- that's dealt with then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, one last thing, it's this attestation has been uploaded into e-court under document ID 0684-4197. It was provisionally admitted pending uploading into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we need it to replace the -- the other one, the one that's not signed off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you repeat the ID number again, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the ERN number. Or is it -- ID number, yes. I give further instructions to Madam Registrar soon. Any other matter? If not, then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] P14 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's P1469. Okay. We need page 19 in B/C/S, and page 12, the bottom part, in English. Also, we need the bottom part of B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, in paragraph -- or, rather, on the second paragraph from the bottom of the page, and in the English version the last two lines on the page, we read the following: "By the end of March, 1995, the Herzegovina Corps Command shall plan operations for reaching the Neretva River valley, termed Krivaja 95, and for reaching the coast-line in the Prevlaka-Cavtat sector, called More 95?" We see that Krivaja 95 was one of the tasks of the Herzegovina Corps. Was it customary to give the same name to different operations or is it more likely based on your experience, that the Drina Corps chose a name for the operation independently and chose the name Drina 95?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a directive, certain operations are assigned code-names, and different operations and different tasks always must have different names. I do not know who it was in the Drina Corps who chose the name Krivaja for this operation here. As far as I remember, in the directive, no one operation with which the Drina Corps was tasked was called Krivaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we please get the last page of this document in both languages. In B/C/S, it's the previous page. And I need item 8 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here we see that Directive 7, signed by Dr. Radovan Karadzic, stipulates that corps commanders decisions for -- must be sent for approval to the VRS Main Staff commander seven days before the operation. If the commander of the Main Staff was not informed, who would be the one to blame in context of the Krivaja operation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander who did not submit the combat documents for a certain operation for approval as mentioned here in this item 8 of the directive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask for clarification, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Obradovic, at page 3, line 5, you say: "As far as I remember, in the directive, no one operation with which the Drina Corps was tasked was called Krivaja." The Krivaja that we saw now on this directive, it's related to Herzegovina Corps? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, so you have my response. [Interpretation] Could we now get Exhibit P1465. It's a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, we see that this is an order for active combat activities of the Drina Corps Command dated the 2nd of July, 1995. We see "Krivaja 95" in the heading. Is it true that the Main Staff of the VRS is not mentioned among the recipients?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is sent to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, the 1st Bratunac Infantry Brigade, the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, the 1st Light Infantry Brigade. I don't remember what BR stands for. And the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade as well as the 5th Mixed Artillery Regiment. The Main Staff is not [Realtime transcript read in error "in the"] mentioned. It could be the Birac Light Infantry Brigade, it just occurred to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just for my understanding, could command of the Drina Corps in any way give orders to the top level? I mean, they were informed about this, isn't it? I mean, why would I expect an order by the Drina Corps to go up rather than down in the line of hierarchy? I'm just missing the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, they received a copy of this order, so what's, then, the use -- at least whether they received it or not, it says at the end of the document that they -- that they received it, that it was sent to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will clarify that with the witness with the next question then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, is it true that, in keeping with Directive 7, the Drina Corps Command was supposed to send this order to the Main Staff of the VRS for approval?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But we see that the heading reads "order," and an order is sent to subordinate units. On the last page, there should be a mention of the one meant to approve this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, could I ask a clarification of your previous answer. You said that the Main Staff would have been -- would have to approve this. I wonder whether they also would have to approve it if the order was given pursuant to instructions or orders that came from the Main Staff. Then there would be no need to approve. Or would there be such need?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in practice, all decisions and plans in order to execute combat actions are approved by the superior officer. If it's in the topographical map, then in the upper right-hand corner would be written "decision by" so-and-so and then "approved by" such and such a person, and then in the right-hand lower corner, it would be signed by the commander who planned the activities. His signature would be there. And so the text of the order itself should be reviewed in order to have it approved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may miss the point. Planning an operation is not the same as executing an operation, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The directive orders the Drina Corps to carry out a certain operation under a certain code-name, when the time comes to implement that task. Up until that time they would have carried out all the preparations, the planning, organising, materiel logistical support, and then the documents pursuant to which they are going to be executing the operation are then submitted to the superior command for approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we look at Directive 7/1, please. This is P1470, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see this is a document of the 31st March of 1995 from the Main Staff of Army of Republika Srpska, directive for further operations, operative number 7/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at page 5 in both versions in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 5.3. There's no need to read the whole thing. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The tasks here are those intended for the Drina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this directive, the document by the Main Staff of the VRS, does not provide for any kind of actions in relation to the enclaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's just not true on the face of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then assist Mr. Lukic in referring to the exact place where it is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It says in the first couple of lines: "Prevent enemy breakthrough along selected operative tactical axes ... persistent defence and active combat actions ..." and -- "on the north-west part of the front and around the enclaves ..." So it is anticipating combat actions as Directive 7 did, around the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was not artfully posed but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please do it artfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is it correct that the VRS directive does not provide for the entry of the forces into the enclaves, the capture of the enclaves, the separation of the enclaves, that that is not the task that is issued to the Drina Corps? Is that how you interpret it? Because we see here what -- actually what do you see from this part of Directive 7/1? What was the task the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This directive in paragraph 5.3 does not contain such an assignment. The emphasis here is on persistent defence and active actions in order to die down certain forces. But the focus is to carry out the operation Spreca first and -- in the first stage. And then in the second stage of the operation, to reach the Vlasenica-Kladanj line and then regroup forces and in joint action with the East Bosnia, 1st Krajina and the PVO forces, these forces are defined by the directive as the main force of the army. In the second and third phases of the operation is infiltrating strong groups into the enemy rear and introducing strong army mechanised forces, execute an attack in the general direction of Kalesija-Dubrava-Tuzla, and reach the village of Serici, Zivinice, Jasicak, Ravno hill positions as soon as possible, thereby cutting off forces of the 2nd Corps of the B and H Army south of that line. And then support here is mentioned from the air force and the PVO, and the corps IKM is to be decided by the corps commander. Therefore, in this directive the Drina Corps comprises the main body of the force together with the 1st Krajina Corps, the East Bosnia Corps, the air force and the anti-aircraft defence, i.e., the PVO. In 5.5 here - could you please bring the page back - it talks about the rest of the forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witnesses says something about 5.5, we would like to have 5.5 on the English screen -- in English on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 5.5, the rest of the VRS forces, comprised by the 2nd Krajina Corps, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, the Herzegovina Corps, colon, and then the task is given, plan and execute tasks given in Directive number 7. So these three corps would be entrusted with the rest of the assignments from Directive 7, whereas the other ones that I mentioned before are going to be proceeding according to the tasks noted in the Directive 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the corps that the witness mentioned were too fast to repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the names of the corps you mentioned last.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the auxiliary forces or for the main force?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think for the -- the main forces. The assignments in Directive 7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The auxiliary forces are 5.5. That is the 2nd Krajina Corps, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and the Herzegovina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you now give the names of the other ones. The other ones who were supposed to further plan and execute what is found in Directive 7.1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Directive 7/1, the main body of the force comprises the 1st Krajina Corps, the East Bosnia Corps, the Drina Corps, and the air force and anti-aircraft defence forces. These were the forces that were supposed to take part in the operation of strategic importance, carrying the code-name Sadejstvo, co-ordinated action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I return for a second to the previous document. That is, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just clarify one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the gentleman can see 5.3 again on his screen because the name of the operation is Spreca 95. I think ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The general couldn't hear me. That's what he was ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What you said just now, Sadejstvo, you meant Spreca 95?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Spreca tasks were supposed to be carried out by the Drina Corps before launching the Sadejstvo 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I would have -- we just looked a minute ago to the order for active combat activities, operation number 1 issued by the Command of the Drina Corps, 2nd of July, 1995. That was the one which was not addressed to the Main Staff, although the Main Staff was to receive a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's P1465.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- copy. You told us that this should have been sent for approval to the Main Staff first. Now, if the Main Staff is informed about this order by a copy sent to it, and if there would have been any disapproval or any criticism on it not having been sent for approval first, what would be the response by the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly, if it was sent, and if there are any corrections in the documents to be made that were planned and drafted by the Drina Corps, then this is something that would be corrected in the Main Staff. If not, approval would be given to proceed according to the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there not be a message: Hey, you guys down there, you are giving an order which has not been approved yet. You should refrain from doing that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I cannot really go into that because I wasn't present. What I'm talking about is the way it should be according to the rules. As for what actually happened, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm still confused. Is this in accordance with the rules? It says nowhere, We are seeking your approval. They're issuing orders. And you told us that that should have been approved first before giving such orders. So it seems to be not in accordance with the rules, as you described them to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you didn't understand. They draft the documents formally the way it should be according to the instructions on the work of the staffs and commands, and they draft the text. They represent the decision graphically on a topographical map after that. If there are no objections or remarks, then they are told to proceed according to the documents which they sent. If there are any remarks or objections, then corrections would be made, and then the task would be carried out according to the corrected documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now do I then have to understand the 2nd of July document, which we looked at earlier, to be sent for approval rather than to be issued to the subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A copy of the document would remain at the corps command. Another copy would be sent to the Main Staff. If approval is received to proceed according to the documents, then the document would be photocopied and submitted to the subordinate units, and those who are supposed to take part in the execution of the assignment would be given their assignments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, if finally, this order would be executed -- no. Let me rephrase my question. First, this order would not be delivered to the subordinate units until after approval would have been received. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how it should be, according to the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, would that approval be given in writing, or could it also be given in any other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An approval can be given via the communications devices, or it can be issued in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So just a radio communication would have been sufficient to approve so that the order could be further executed. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now I am a bit confused. Because you said earlier that the approval was given by the higher level of command by a signature on the topographical map. That means not in normal writing, not by telegram, not by phone call, nor not by Motorola or whatever. What is true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The instruction on the working map defines the graphic representation and the narrative part and so on. But, in practice, it can happen that the organs of the staff sector inspect a plan and suggest to the commander that everything is all right, so that the commander, who may not even be at the Main Staff, orally approves the use of these documents that were sent to the Main Staff by the subordinate commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand, if no correction is received on any of the points, and if an oral approval would have been given through radio communication, you could just go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Earlier in a trial I was explaining the role of the staff sector in inspecting the documents of the subordinate commands in the context of approving a decision. When they inspect all of that and inform the commander or the chief of Main Staff that it is okay, then he approves. If there are -- if corrections must be made, then the documents are sent back for further processing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we clarify the Defence's position on this? It's incumbent upon them to tell their -- to put the case to the witness so the suggestion -- I can't tell but it appears to be that the Main Staff did not approve this plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was at least what I understood to be the suggestion implied in the questions. Mr. Lukic, could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will follow with my questions so it will be clear, I think. I would rather the witness testify rather than me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the witness can -- the witness cannot testify about the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our position that this document never reached Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then perhaps I should have let you first ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the witness. Perhaps that was not a very wise decision. But let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I tried to do. Okay. Thank you. Let's have the last page of this document on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me first ask you, General, do you know if this document ever made it to the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can it be inferred from this document that, at the same time it was sent to the Main Staff of the VRS, was copied seven-fold and these copies were delivered to the forward command post number 1 of the KDK and the rest of them as listed here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can read to the left of the signature block that this was typed in two copies and delivered to: One, original, in the archives of the Drina Corps Command; and two, Main Staff of the VRS. Below that there's an additional remark saying, "seven copies made and delivered to: Forward command post number 1 of the Drina Corps Command; the 1st Zvornik" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you don't have to read out that list. We see that there are seven units mentioned there. Please proceed. I mean, proceed with your answer. The question was whether you can infer from this document that, if I understood you well, Mr. Lukic, that simultaneously the copies were sent to the Main Staff and to the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you answer, General.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. We saw in the heading of the document the date of the 2nd of July, I think. I don't know when the subordinate units received it. I'd have to see some document of the subordinate units to be able to tell whether it was received simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now focus on this remark: "Seven copies made and delivered to ..." This refers to the past; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this document of the 2nd of July tells us that, at that point in time, it already been delivered.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a reference to a past time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I move on or you have more questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one more question. The same - at least in the English translation - is said for the Main Staff of the VRS. Would that mean that they would have -- it would have been delivered to them already and that the original was already delivered to the archive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably. This narrative part of the decision of the commander of the Drina Corps is accompanied by a graphic representation on a topographic map. It cannot be sent over a coded communications channel. You would have to give that to a courier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that because it says "seven copies delivered to" that it had been delivered already. Now I ask you whether the words "typed in two copies and delivered to" would not then have the same meaning, that it had been delivered already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it would apply to all of this. This is either a note saying that one copy goes to the Main Staff and another to the archives. And, yes, it says "delivered to." It doesn't say "to be delivered to." So this is a reference to the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this is a totally new concept for me, that you sent a document to say that the same document was sent or delivered. That is puzzling me highly, just for you to know, Mr. Lukic. And I see that the typewriting seems to be similar for this last portion in the original compared to the previous text above the signature. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, does this document tell us that even if it was delivered to the Main Staff of the VRS, and since we see that the document was drafted on the 2nd of July, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1995. Could counsel please repeat the last part of his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're invited to repeat the last part of your question. But if you want to consult with your -- if there's any need to consult with Mr. Mladic, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that even if this document was delivered to the Main Staff of the VRS and simultaneously to the seven addresses stated below, they didn't wait for an approval of the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible if the one who signed the order was sure that the Main Staff would approve this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment of patience, please. I must consult my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have on page -- yeah, page, I think, 17, line 8, we have an English translation that the document Krivaja 95 was drafted on July 2nd. And I don't know if that's a translation issue or not. But there's no mention of drafted like there was on the directive. We -- we have a date of July 2nd on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which does not exclude that it was drafted that day but at least it's dated the 2nd of July. Mr. Lukic, you would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I don't think that in the answer of the witness it -- there's any reason to revisit that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I get clarification, Mr. Lukic, before you go on. Page 17, line 15, that last question you put to the witness, you said: "... they didn't wait for an approval of the Main Staff of the VRS." I want to get -- and the witness said in response: "That is the possible if the one who signed the order was sure that the Main Staff would approve this." Now when you -- when you -- when you say that, sir, wait -- they didn't wait before what happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, the question did not -- they didn't wait to do what or to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To start with the action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That was not part of the -- did you understand the question in that way, Witness, that they would not wait to start executing the order. Is that what your answer relates to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked before it was sent to the subordinate units in accordance with the heading. And we saw the date of the 2nd there. So that it's clear that they didn't wait for a response from the Main Staff before they sent it to the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you sent it to the -- sent it to the subordinate units without any reservation, it would mean that they would act in accordance with the order. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about any direct contacts between President Karadzic and General Krstic in connection with this operation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only -- I know of it only from an appearance of President Karadzic on TV. And he said - I'm paraphrasing now - that he ordered General Krstic to implement the Srebrenica operation. Or that he -- he ordered him to plan it. But that was said on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that General Mladic received the required documents to the -- for this operation of the Drina Corps only on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that because I arrived at the Main Staff only on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why I asked you. You may have learned of it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to put a follow-up question to the witness. You were asked about direct contacts between President Karadzic and General Krstic. Do you know anything about any direct contacts between General Mladic and General Krstic, in connection with this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, one of your questions has not received an answer yet. The witness said that he doesn't know that General Mladic received the required documents for this operation only on the 13th of July because he arrived only at the 17th at the Main Staff. Then your question was whether he learned about it later. And that question has not been answered yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did answer. You may not have heard it. I said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was not on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] I think it's a break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly is time for the break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'll take a break of 20 minutes, Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time to give the further instructions to Madam Registrar in relation to P387, which was admitted conditionally pending attestation and declaration. Doc ID 0684-4197 should replace the English version of P387, which is now without attestation and declaration. And I hereby confirm that, once this is replaced, that P387 is now finally admitted into evidence. The attestation and declaration are not in the B/C/S translation but that is usual practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I need make one correction in the transcript. And maybe we should have P1465 on our screens as well, the first page. The correction in transcript is -- should be -- be made on the page 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 4. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was in line 7, so we know -- what we are talking about. That, in this document, on our screen, P1465, and my question was: Is it true that the Main Staff of the VRS is not mentioned among the recipients? Then the answer registered in line 13 is: "The Main Staff is in the mentioned." And the answer was: The Main Staff is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Among the addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among addressees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although the Main Staff is mentioned at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- very bottom of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- this is only for addressees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is I think there's no disagreement, whatever -- of whatever kind as to question and answer and the content of the document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, one question out of context. I was going through my questions now at the break. You were asked about Warrant Officer Zeljkovic yesterday. He was one of those who signed the directive. Actually, he typed it out.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that he is a sergeant. I think that's what it says there, sergeant first class.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Staff-Sergeant Zeljkovic, who was he subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Staff-Sergeant Zeljkovic was in the logistics sector, and I think he was in the technical service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was trained for data entry into the computer. Perhaps I'm mistaken about the technical service and the logistics sector. I'm not quite sure, but I think that's where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I wanted to ask you something about the 10th Sabotage Detachment. This unit was discussed. We have that in the diagram. In the professional sense, to whom was the 10th Sabotage Detachment subordinated? In the professional sense.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the professional sense, the sabotage detachment was subordinated to the chief of the intelligence administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1995, who was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Petar Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who was the immediate superior to Petar Salapura?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was part of the security and intelligence administration headed by General -- Major-General Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct -- actually, you can tell me. Who suggests the use of the 10th Sabotage Detachment to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that has to do with the activities of that -- proposals for the use of that unit is -- are given by the chief of the administration. Just as the chief of the combat arms of armoured units or artillery would propose the use of artillery or their own combat arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I ask -- the chief of the administration, in this context, would that be General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Tolimir is at the centre -- at the head of the sector. The sector had two administrations: The intelligence administration and the security administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, would it be Colonel Salapura himself who would -- let me just check. Could you give a name to the -- where you said the head of the administration? Who would be that -- who would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The chief of the intelligence administration was Colonel Petar Salapura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if the 10th Sabotage Detachment were to be resubordinated to the Drina Corps, who would it answer to? To the commander of the Main Staff or to the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each unit that is resubordinated, including the 10th Sabotage Detachment, or the sabotage detachment, when it reports to the commander of the unit to which it is being resubordinated, until the time the task is completed is under the command and executes assignments of the commander to whom it is resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, in this case, that would be the commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if the unit is resubordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who commands the military police of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander to whom the police brigade under -- under whom the police brigade is, and that would be the commander of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let's say that there is a military police platoon in the battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By establishment, a battalion does not have a police component.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I found in somebody's answer earlier that it does, but thank you for the correction. So what would be the first lowest-ranking unit that would have a military police component?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brigade. A regiment or a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how does the reporting, then, proceed? From the unit -- from the commander of the military police unit within the brigade, who does that go to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not a komandant, it's a komandir because it is usually a military police company so all the reporting is given to the komandant, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The commander of what?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the professional sense, it would go to the superior at the corps command or the intelligence organ -- actually, the security organ, excuse me. Mostly for those tasks that have to do with counter-intelligence work and tasks of -- of a criminal investigation nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you know - and if you don't, just say you don't know - so how detailed are the reports that come from that level to Colonel Salapura?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, if you can, all right; but if not, just say that you cannot, that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this is not a part of the exhibit admitted as your statement, can we look at 1D1134, in e-court, please. 1D1134 should be the transcript dated the 31st of March, 2011, from the Tolimir case. We need to look at page 106 of this transcript, and that would correspond to transcript page 12194.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. McCloskey asked you in line 9: [In English] "Q. And my question about prisoners of war, we have seen military police guarding and sometimes questioning prisoners of war. Would that be a part of their duty? "A. Yes. Probably that was done by members of the crime departments on the strength of the military police." [Interpretation] And would you stand by this part of your statement today? Would you stand by this part of your statement today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they're the most professional ones in order to take statements and in order to question the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your question was, does he stand by that statement. He hasn't answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer with a yes or no. Would you agree with this part of your statement today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stand by the part that pertains to the taking of statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about guarding?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Guarding is not the exclusive task of the military police. Any fighter could do that job. And usually members of the military police unit, even when they're recruited, need to be a bit more capable than just regular fighters. So that it's not efficient to use that personnel for guard-duty assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But would you agree that the military police is trained both for guard duty and for escorting prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in peacetime and -- however, in wartime, all fighters can -- can do that; but as far as bringing people in and questioning them, that would be their assignment, their task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is the role of the security organ and the intelligence organ in the professional sense? For example, as it relates to the military police in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security and the intelligence organ? Well, the intelligence organ is busy with intelligence-gathering about the opposing side --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we're talking about the military police, what sort of professional responsibility do they have or don't have, putting forward suggestions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a formation in the brigade which is called the reconnaissance company. In the professional sense, it is commanded by the chief of the intelligence sector, the assistant commander for intelligence. And the chief of security, in the professional sense, is in charge of the military police company, for their training, sending them for training, for counter-intelligence work, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is the person who commands that unit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both units are under the command of the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know Momir Nikolic from the Bratunac Brigade, right? You heard of him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of him in connection with a trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was his immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade commander. And along professional lines, that is, the lines of intelligence, the chief of intelligence affairs of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic from the Drina Corps, who was his direct superior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander. And along professional lines of security and counter-intelligence, the chief of the security administration of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the chief of the intelligence and security sector of the Main Staff, General Tolimir, cannot issue an order to a military police battalion of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends if he was given authority to do so by his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'd have to look at P1783. It's your testimony from the Tolimir case which was admitted as your statement. My question may have been less than precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 108, please, in e-court. That should correspond to transcript page 12196. Then we'll need the following page, 12196. Line 24, I'll read it out: [In English] "The chief of an administration may not issue a task to the military police battalion within the Drina Corps. This is within the authority of the commander. However, through the security organ, in the professional aspect" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "However, through the security organ, in the professional aspect, he can help general, professional, and specialised training in order to enable the military police to perform their tasks in a professional way. But when we are talking about assigning tasks, that is something done by the commander." [Interpretation] My question may have been insufficiently clear. Do you stand by this statement of yours in the Tolimir case, when you say that he was in no position to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by that. But you gave an example of brigades and asked about a military police company and a recon company. They are in the exclusive authority of the brigade commander. So only the commander is authorised to command these units. Talking about professional lines, they have to do with specific types of tasks, but that does not involve commanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that Colonel Beara from the security administration, as part of the sector headed by General Tolimir, could not issue orders to the military police battalion of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same as in the previous example. It's exclusively up to the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All this applies to the military police companies of the Zvornik and Bratunac Brigades; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are commanded by the brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're done with the military police. Now I'll briefly deal with the period before the operations in and around the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica. Do you know that at a certain point the Main Staff of the VRS - that is, the security of the Main Staff - was attacked from these enclaves?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second half of June 1995, before I returned from my sick-leave, I think it was on the 26th of June, nine sabotage and terrorist groups were infiltrated from Zepa and the surrounding areas. Then the communications regiment and the motorised regiment had seven dead and 12 wounded. Among the wounded, there was also Major Knezevic. I don't remember his first name. But he was a member of the Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far was the Main Staff of the VRS from Zepa?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15, 20 kilometres. But those groups were very close to the Main Staff, which was at Crna Rijeka. As a result, the soldiers of the -- these units providing security to the Main Staff, that is, the 67th Communications Regiment and the 65th Protection Regiment, came to harm.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could counsel please start over with his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please re-start your question, Mr. Lukic. Interpreters did not catch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now first need P23. It's a demilitarisation agreement for Srebrenica signed by General Ratko Mladic, as we see, then General Sefer Halilovic, in the presence of General Philippe Morillon. Could we please get the last page with the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you worked at the Main Staff and did your job, what -- how did -- what do you think, how did the Serbian side interpret this agreement? Were the persons who signed it in such positions as to be able to bind all three sides? Was General Mladic's signature binding for the Serbian side or Halilovic's signature for the Bosniak side?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signatures of these two persons from the VRS and the BH army were binding. General Mladic was not to touch the protected zone. Sefer Halilovic was to conduct a demilitarisation. The same applies to General Morillon. And no combat activities were allowed from the protected zone. The precondition was demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the protected zone was never demilitarised; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't. Due to the huge losses, within three years after the signature of this agreement, Serbian villages around Bratunac suffered a lot, and even soldiers of the VRS came to harm. I spoke about the events before July - that is, on the 26th of June - nine sabotage and terrorist groups were infiltrated. You know what that meant, in terms of fear among the Serbian population. They were -- people were killed and their property looted and destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, part of your question is about who was competent to sign for whom, which seems to be a legal issue. That's one. We have submissions of the parties and despite the criticism by the Defence that we were making up our minds too early, what we wanted to have is a proper understanding of the context of many questions put to witnesses as they are today. And, second, the remainder of the evidence you are eliciting now seems to be very repetitious. We have heard that many, many times, and we did not understand from the re-examination of the witnesses by the Prosecution that there was great dispute about such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It is fundamentally uncontested [Realtime transcript read in error "contested"] this -- these issues as I stated in the opening statement and many times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if it will be the third time or the fourth time, but I think it is now the tenth time that we hear this evidence, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry if I was not clear, but my main intention is to elicit from this gentleman how VRS side understood the signature of Mr. Morillon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you should ask that question to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well ... could you assist me in where exactly you did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in -- on page 31, line 12. I said, I asked: While you worked at the Main Staff and did your job --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said, Were the signatures binding, and you asked about Mladic and Halilovic. You didn't say a word about Morillon --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Maybe it's not registered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Morillon was not a party to the agreement, a witness to the agreement, so focussed questions in that respect I would not mind but -- and that does not in any way change what I said after that, that what happened, attacks on villages, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I see that -- sorry. Now I see that part of my question is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least it was not dealt with in the answer, so then would you have insisted on a complete answer to your questions if you were focussed [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the witness also dealt with Mr. Morillon in his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see where he does so. These two persons he talks about. Then he talks about Mladic in the end. He says, "the same applies to General Morillon." What now "the same" is, is not clear because for Mladic and for Halilovic there were apparently different obligations. So it's at least -- well, let's say, in a positive way it's totally unclear what you asked and what you wanted to elicit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try to clarify. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I started that observation with legal opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I'm asking the gentleman how it was seen on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But then please, very precise, what was seen, of course, Morillon was -- had a command position, et cetera, but please try to focus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I hope the transcript will clear it up, but I'm quoted as saying that it's "fundamentally contested" when it is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard you say that this was uncontested. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard this discussion, General. Therefore my question will be short. How did the Serbian side understand the role of General Morillon when he signed this agreement as a witness? Did you understand that UNPROFOR was thereby assuming some duties or not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We understood it the following way. General Morillon, as representative of the peacekeeping forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina who have a neutral status, was to monitor whether this agreement was honoured and implemented. That's why their forces were deployed around Zepa. I'm still convinced that the UN failed to create a protected zone --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Did not create a protected zone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so that the 28th Division could conduct raids from there and return there after those raids unharmed. And I'm speaking about the 28th Division of the BH army. That's how we understood that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I've finished with this area, so if you have any further questions, Your Honour, I would move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I have no further questions apart from that -- what we now know is what the witness believe happened. We have not talked about obligations, and we have not a clear analysis -- and perhaps we could not expect this from this witness on obligations and duties of all -- of the two parties and the UNPROFOR as a witness to this, which was assigned certain tasks. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about this operation directed at Zepa now. Was it planned by the Main Staff; do you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that in my previous testimony as well. This was an active that was planned at the Command of the Drina Corps, and the control of that operation was entrusted to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the action was planned at the Main Staff and that you were supposed to monitor the development of the action? Could you tell us a little bit about it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had it been an operation that was supposed to have been controlled by the Main Staff, then the planning, the organisation would also have been carried out by the Main Staff. The actual organisation of the course of the operation was something that was monitored by the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You returned on the 17th of July, 1995. So, in that case, you would have personally taken part in the operation, the overseeing of it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, you were asked also about the humanitarian convoys, so that would be the next area that I would ask you to focus on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to need a new document in e-court, 1D1100. As you can see, this is the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska. We need to look at the next page. This first decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you can see here, this is a decision on forming a state committee for co-operation with the United Nations and international humanitarian organisations. First of all, would you agree with me that when you were explaining the humanitarian convoys issue, you did not know that such a state committee was formed and that you did not know what its responsibilities were?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about the committee, but I was not sure about its composition, and I did not know what exactly its responsibilities were.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could all extra microphones be switched off, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This decision was adopted on the 14th of March, 1995. We will come to the signatories. It was signed by the president of the republic, Dr. Radovan Karadzic. We need to look at Article 6 now, please. Article 6 of the decision which states: "Permits for the movement of convoys and employees of the UN and humanitarian organisations on the territory of Republika Srpska shall be issued by the co-ordinating body for humanitarian operations, pursuant to committee decisions." Article 7 states: "The committee shall adopt special rules of procedure for issuing permits for the movement of convoys and employees of the UN and humanitarian organisations on the territory of Republika Srpska." In Article 3 - we need to go back a little bit - it states: "Decisions and orders from the committee's jurisdiction are binding for all state organs of Republika Srpska." We now need to look at Article 8. We will also see the signatory, but Article 8 states: "The committee shall submit a quarterly report on its work to the president of the republic." We can see that the date is the 14th of March, 1995, and that it's signed by the president of the republic, Dr. Radovan Karadzic. Of course, the army checked the convoys in the field; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Authorised persons from the units carried out controls as determined by the commanders who -- through whose territory the convoys were passing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware how General Ratko Mladic carried out the instructions or the requests of the committee? We can see on the documents that he would put "yes" or "no" on the documents. Do you know whether this "yes" or "no" was his decision, or was that something that he received as to which convoy should be let through and which one should not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anything about the communication of General Mladic and others that he was communicating with. All I know are documents that would come from the sector initialed by him. I don't know on which basis such decisions were made though.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to look at an earlier decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to look at 65 ter P14596, in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please check the number. That can't be correct. It can't be 65 ter and P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 65 ter. It's 65 ter number [Interpretation] 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Without the P.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Without P, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we can see that even though at the top it says "Supreme Headquarters of the Army of Republic of Srpska," it's obvious that the document was issued by the president of the republic, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, which we can see from the signature. And this is also how the interpreter -- how the translators understood it when they were translating it into English. At the bottom of the page in English, it says: "Therefore, I have made the following decision ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stay on the same page in the B/C/S, and can we move to the next page in English version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed there is only one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it's 65 ter number. So probably we would have to ask the Prosecution to upload the next page. In English at least. But I will just read one paragraph, after this, what we already have translated in English, it's under number 1 what we can see in B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It states here: "Therefore, I have made the following decision: All permits for the movement of humanitarian convoys, as well as supply convoys for UNPROFOR, will be issued from the office of the Supreme Commander. Before that, the cabinet, the office, will obtain your opinion and other representative opinions." This document is from December 1994. Did you know that already at that time, Dr. Karadzic's office was the only institution that could decide about the passage of humanitarian convoys and UNPROFOR convoys?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, in 1994, December 1994, I was at the western front, so this is the first time that I'm seeing this document. But it does state in paragraph 2 that all the correspondence of the VRS with international organisations is to proceed through the office of the Supreme Commander. For that purpose, a special fax line will be set up that will be constantly on duty, and that fax was the fax of Colonel Milos Djurdjic that was dedicated to that. From the Supreme Commander's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not in dispute that there were controls and also restrictions on the passage of some convoys. Did you ever hear that convoys that were supposed to be humanitarian convoys transported ammunition and weaponry through the territory of Republika Srpska for the other side?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's an obvious example of that, that I saw at this Tribunal in the Karadzic case when he showed a document during the cross-examination where a member of the peacekeeping forces addresses the Defence Ministry of the B and H Army, stating that in the previous convoy, oxygen tanks incorrectly -- contained incorrectly packed ammunition so that any shifting of the bottles could reveal the presence of ammunition, which did not happen, but he issued a warning that this should not happen again in future and that these -- this -- these items should be packed properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at 1D -- in e-court, yes, actually, that is 1D1101. [In English] Or maybe it's break time so we can continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will continue after the break. But, first, the witness should be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were speaking about a document but I think we'll call it up later. This is the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We see in the signature block the name of Sefer Halilovic, Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command. And he says it is necessary to approve as many oxygen bottles as possible. They will be transported to Zagreb, and they will be used at the front in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we get 1D1104 in e-court, please. This is not the document. 1D1104 is what I need.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document uploaded under this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Then we'll go back to the previous document. We don't need this one, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I inquire, before you continue, to what extent or where there is dispute about the oxygen bottle incident. So that we can focus on -- because that such an incident happened, whether or not staged, whether or not -- I don't know, but is there a dispute about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. Nor is there dispute about the bullets and the flour incident or the other few incidents about this sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Why not at least agree on this as a basis for any possible further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no dispute that humanitarian aid was used for smuggling ammunition and weaponry, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least that there were such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hmm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree that there were a few incidents and that the VRS has every right to control those and did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My mistake was that I would just like to see 1D1103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid problems in the future, could you make a short list of these incidents so that the parties agree that these incidents took place and to the extent they can agree on whether they were used for smuggling, that we have that somewhere on the record. Mr. Lukic, are you willing to stipulate these matters, together with Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then that may save quite some time in court. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In any way, we will just propose for those two documents to be admitted into evidence, 1D1101 and 1D1103. So we have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, I take it, then, Mr. McCloskey. Madam Registrar, for these two documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1101 receives number D334, Your Honours. And document 1D1103 receives number D335, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will not ask any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me now return to the time when you returned to the Main Staff. I'll ask you about Srebrenica. Did you know, while you were at the Main Staff, how many prisoners had been taken in the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we should return to P1470. This is Directive 7/1 again, but the context is very different. In the B/C/S, I need page 6, and it's the same page in English. Paragraph 4. And it's item 6.3 in B/C/S. It seems that we need the following page in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that item 6.3, at the bottom of the page, reads: "When using communications, means of communications" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We don't see where counsel is reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seems to be second paragraph of item 6.3, the fourth line, "When using communications systems ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said paragraph 4 on this page in English version. Yes, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "When using communications systems adhere strictly to cryptographic protection procedures and limit the use of handheld and other non-secure radio equipment to the essential minimum, taking care that the enemy is definitely not listening in. Plan and organise the work of a decoy radio network at the level of VRS Main Staff and the corps commands." What does this mean, this use of decoy radio networks?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to protect our own intentions and plans and deceive the enemy, decoy radio networks were set up with a certain number, a certain quantity of devices to confuse the enemy so that he gets a wrong image of the number of units. Because each device would simulate a separate command, or a separate unit. In these decoy radio networks, orders were issued to direct the attention of the enemy in the wrong direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if participants in a conversation introduced themselves as being somebody else?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the ones operating these decoy radio networks took care for their activity to be as convincing as possible. They would issue orders from the commands to units; whereas, in reality, there were no such commands and no such units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1577 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I ask a question before we move to the next document. In the paragraph following the one you read, there are strict conditions on the secrecy of the planned operations. Do you know what the reason was for that, that even the ICRC could not freely move around, UNHCR, UNPROFOR. They all should be -- should be forbidden any free movement. Perhaps we should go to the next page in B/C/S. Was this common or what was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this a question for me? This says, Mr. President, that all decisions about the intention to conduct operations are protected so that the enemy don't learn about it. It says specifically the movement of members of UNPROFOR and workers of UNHCR, ICRC and so on, whose activities have been noted by intelligence. Which means that our intelligence has a list of persons belonging to these organisations but who, in fact, conduct activities directed against us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And journalists? During the operation? Was there anything to hide during the operation? That journalists were not allowed to report on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I suppose that among them too there were people known to intelligence and not favourably inclined to us. These corps mentioned here made up the majority of the forces in this planned operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know of the existence of any lists of those who you said were unfavorable to you, for example, among the journalists. Because all journalists apparently were banned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't receive -- I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me now in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I heard it now. I did not have such a list, and probably the intelligence organ had no need to send me one. Such lists would sooner be forwarded to the units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I didn't ask whether you had such a list. I asked you whether you -- you knew about the existence of such lists.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In conversations, I heard intelligence guys mention such lists. It's part of their counter-intelligence activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm addressing both parties. Is there any evidence about the existence of specifically those persons under -- in these groups that would be suspected of not sticking to their mission but to act unfavourably? And I'm talking about UNHCR, ICRC, journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any -- of any lists about -- about that. I do remember comments about individual journalists made over the time period. But lists, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. If you say you would need more time to think about it or to ask members of your team, then, of course, I would accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would have to check probably EDS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I'm not aware right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Because the witness relies on it, therefore I wondered whether there was any evidence which would support his -- his evidence, although he was assuming, I think, a few things without actual knowledge. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I consult with the client for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may, if he uses his voice at low volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Low volume. Low volume means not audible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We are finished with this document. We can move on. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I need P1577.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we can see on the screen in front of us a document of the 24th of October, 1994, from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.
